name: Can I use an attached ADU for rental income in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: If I build an attached ADU, can I legally rent it out separately, or are there restrictions on who can live there?
mainEntity.text: If I build an attached ADU, can I legally rent it out separately, or are there restrictions on who can live there?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached ADU is often designed for separate occupancy, which makes it attractive for rental income, family members, or long-term guests. However, the unit must be approved as a legal ADU and built to the correct standards, including independent living facilities and proper permits. Homeowners should also confirm whether the property has any HOA restrictions, deed conditions, or site-specific rules that affect renting. The design should support privacy, code compliance, and efficient operations, because a rental unit needs durable finishes, sound separation, and a clean circulation path. It is smart to plan the electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems with future use in mind so maintenance is straightforward. The most common mistake is treating the ADU like a casual room addition and only later trying to make it function as a real unit. If rental income is the goal, the layout, finishes, and utility strategy should all be built around that use from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: In many cases, yes, an attached ADU can be rented separately if it is approved as a legal ADU and meets local rules. The unit must usually have its own entrance, kitchen, and bathroom, and the owner should verify whether the property has any deed restrictions, HOA limits, or local rental rules.
